searchText: deployment hardening — planned versus actual original recovery plan the recovery wave intentionally froze application code and focused only on production transport. the plan required named remote phases, safe diagnostics, bounded fetch retries, repair of detached or stale branch state, exact sha validation, preservation of canonical activation, public verification, and a release canary. what was observed two consecutive pushes reached github actions but failed in the same opaque single ssh deployment step before the running service exposed the new reconciliation route. the product release itself had already passed 115 isolated tests and clean diff hygiene. the public apps, games, and transcribe surfaces remained healthy, proving the failure was deployment side rather than a public outage. the original workflow bundled repository preparation, activation, and public verification into one ssh action. that made the failure phase invisible. the activation script also proved that git checkout could advance before service restart, so the old public route alone could not tell whether fetch/reset or activation had failed. what was changed only .github/workflows/main.yml was rewritten in the isolated release worktree. the deployment now has four named phases: 1. probe production ssh reachability. 2. prepare exact production checkout. 3. activate canonical production server. 4. verify canonical public release. the checkout phase now validates the expected forty character sha, checks the production git repository, retries only git fetch with bounded backoff, verifies origin/main, repairs detached or stale branch state with checkout b main, cleans the checkout, and verifies a clean exact sha result. a safe err diagnostic prints only phase, exit code, branch, head, and origin/main sha. it never enables shell tracing or prints secrets. activation remains delegated to the existing canonical production activation script. public verification preserves the existing home and tunnel verifiers and adds the new reconciliation route as a deployment canary: an invalid route response proves the new wallet router is not yet running. structural outcome the first workflow rewrite reached 132 lines and was rejected. the second reached 121 lines and was rejected. the final rewrite is 119 lines, preserving readable control flow instead of minifying it. the application release remains unchanged. no commerce, wallet, apps, games, seo, server runtime, or activation source was modified by this recovery wave. remaining action commit the single validated workflow file separately, require remote main freshness, push without force, observe the newly split github actions phases, and verify the public reconciliation canary plus primary public routes.

searchText: phase one — main only convergence the goal is one canonical repository folder, one long lived branch (main), and no valuable work stranded in auxiliary worktrees or historical branches. non negotiable constraints mutate source only under /users/awtsmoos/work/awtsmoos.com. do not create any new branches. preserve every valuable local commit and uncommitted file before deleting branch/worktree references. never force push over unknown remote work. never commit secrets, caches, generated junk, or machine local artifacts merely because they are untracked. keep product source changes whole file only. convergence possibilities detect branches already fully contained in origin/main and delete their local references after verifying no dirty worktree remains. detect branches with unique commits and replay/merge their content into canonical main only after diff review and tests. detect worktrees whose branch commit is already contained upstream but whose filesystem contains uncommitted changes; harvest those diffs into canonical main before removal. detect prunable/missing worktrees and prune their metadata immediately after confirming their branch tips are safe. preserve canonical main's four unique commits. classify the 2,009 canonical local changes by tracked/untracked, top level area, size, and secret risk before any commit. bring origin/main into canonical main only after local work is made durable on main. resolve conflicts in favor of current product truth rather than blindly taking one side. run tests per merged area before publishing. delete merged local branches and obsolete worktrees when their unique commit count against final main is zero.
